s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution
salient_findings: Macular edema resolution after intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Hyperreflective tissues proliferating on retinal vessels on OCTA
Dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography
key_facts: 76-year-old woman presented with macular edema
Treated with 2 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Macular edema completely resolved at 3 months
No recurrence of macular edema
OCTA findings at 6 months showed no abnormality
OCTA findings at 12 months showed hyperreflective tissues on retinal vessels
OCTA findings at 15 months showed increased hyperreflective tissues with angiogenic sprouts
Fluorescein Angiography at 21 months showed dendritic vascular-like structures

shortlist.label: Retinal Angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with macular edema, followed by the development of hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts on OCTA, and dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography, is consistent with Coats Disease, which is characterized by abnormal retinal vascular development and telangiectasia.

rejected.label: Retinal Angiomatosis
rejected.why: Retinal Angiomatosis is a broader term that encompasses several conditions, including Coats Disease, but the specific findings in this case are more consistent with Coats Disease

rejected.label: Von Hippel-Lindau Disease
rejected.why: Von Hippel-Lindau Disease typically presents with retinal and CNS hemangioblastomas, which were not described in this case

rejected.label: Retinal Telangiectasia
rejected.why: Retinal Telangiectasia is a nonspecific term that can be seen in several conditions, including Coats Disease, but the specific pattern of vascular proliferation and angiogenic sprouts in this case is more consistent with Coats Disease

rejected.label: Eales Disease
rejected.why: Eales Disease typically presents with retinal vasculitis and neovascularization, but the pattern of vascular proliferation and the absence of inflammation in this case make it less likely
